title: Prediction
description: One public, dated, attributable prediction and how it resolved.

claim.description: Verbatim quote. Ellipses allowed for trimming, no paraphrase.

context.description: One or two neutral sentences on the setting. No adjectives.

role_at_time.description: What they were when they said it, e.g. 'President, Digital Equipment Corporation'

expertise_domain.description: The field they had a track record in, if any

speaking_in_own_field.description: Was the prediction inside their area of demonstrated expertise?

standing.description: Why anyone listened. practitioner: founder, executive or builder in the domain. researcher: academic or scientist with a publication record. official: elected or appointed public role. commentator: journalist, author, investor or broadcaster with a public audience. publication: an unsigned editorial voice.

audience_at_time.description: Evidence of reach when the claim was made, e.g. follower count, circulation, office held. Required for social-post sources.

made.description: ISO date. Use YYYY or YYYY-MM if day unknown.

venue.description: Where it was said: publication, conference, broadcast

source.description: For type social-post, archive_url is required.

stated.description: Did the predictor give a date or horizon?

date.description: ISO date or year if stated

text.description: The predictor's own words for the horizon, e.g. 'within ten years'

confidence_expressed.description: Predictor's own certainty language, e.g. 'no reason', 'will certainly', '10%'

status.description: Editorial status. Only 'verified' entries are published.

rejection_reason.description: If rejected: misattributed, unverifiable, out of context, joke, private remark
